facts.fact: The Countdown to 2030 report presented by Senegal's health ministry directorates analyses facility data reported through DHIS2 for 2019-2024, including by district and region.

The report states that the share of districts with report completeness of 90% or more was 57% in 2024 for reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health (antenatal care and delivery) in DHIS2, and gives an overall data-quality score of 63% in 2024.

note: Mentions DHIS2 data hosted on University of Oslo servers and planned interoperability for a disease programme, but states no national reporting in service and no existing link.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health and Social Action

note: DHIS2 is listed as the ministry's health information platform, being moved to the SENUM data centre; national reporting, linkage and completeness are not stated.

facts.fact: Senegal's health ministry said it operates a unified national platform based on DHIS2 for health information.
The ministry said the national DHIS2 platform has been extended to epidemiological surveillance, human resources, the supply chain and maternal and perinatal death surveillance.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene

note: An online platform for medicines marketing authorisation; it is not a system for routine health reporting from facilities.
The District Health Information System is cited only as the model; no country-specific health MIS state is given.

facts.fact: Since January 2025 all districts have begun entering health data on the national platform, says the ministry's health information division head.
Ministry official Tidjane Gadjaga says health data completeness rose from under 30% to 80% after unions lifted their data retention in January 2025.

note: No national health reporting system is described.
